messages.subject: Moderated mediation and latent variables
parts:
Hi,

I would like to do a moderated mediation model with latent variables and more specifically the model 15 of Hayes (http://www.afhayes.com/public/templates.pdf). To calculate the conditional direct effect of X on Y, I need to have the variable XV ((product of X and V) in my database. But since all my variables are latent variables, I can't calculate it before estimating the model. Is there a solution to overcome this problem ?
Many thanks for your help.

Hélène

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Moderated mediation and latent variables
parts: I would like to do a moderated mediation model with latent variables and more specifically the model 15 of Hayes (http://www.afhayes.com/public/templates.pdf). To calculate the conditional direct effect of X on Y, I need to have the variable XV ((product of X and V) in my database. But since all my variables are latent variables, I can't calculate it before estimating the model. Is there a solution to overcome this problem ?

You can use the product-indicator approach in lavaan.  The semTools package has a function "orthogonalize" that will help with this, and the help page for the function includes references to read about this method.

You could also use latent moderated structural equations (LMS), which is implemented in Mplus but not lavaan.  If you want to continue using R, the package "nlsem" implements it, but their model specification is not as intuitive as lavaan / Mplus syntax.

Terry

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Moderated mediation and latent variables
parts:
fit_mesure_MLB_mi <- cfa.mi(modele_mesure, data = epd_opi_mi,m=20,estimator = "ML",se="bootstrap", seed=12345)
==> Error in cfa formal argument "se" matched by multiple actual arguments

I assume you are attempting to employ Wu & Jia's (2013) method for indirect effects with missing data (http://dx.doi.org/10.1080/00273171.2013.816235).  As of now, you cannot use bootstrapping in the runMI functions, although I'm not sure that needs to be the case.  Currently, the runMI functions begin by creating a template of a lavaan output object where the pooled MI results can be stored.  The source code creates that template (see lines 50-52) by already specifying the argument se = "none" -- that's why your error message says that there are two matches for the "se" argument (one is yours, one is from the source code).  

I'm not sure why the authors of this function set se = "none" for the template, so I'll bring it to their attention in case that can be changed in the next release. 

Terry

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Moderated mediation and latent variables
parts:
In this case the error is not related to the template used in the runMI code. Instead, R is kicking back an error when an argument in the ... section (other arguments to lavaan) starts with the same letters as an argument to cfa.mi (in this case the seed argument). This can be avoided by specifying the ... section as a list. Note, this error occurs whenever the se argument is specified.

So this causes the same error:
 out <- cfa.mi(HS.model, data=HSMiss, seed = 1234, m = 3, chi="all", se = "standard")

But this works fine:
 out <- cfa.mi(HS.model, data=HSMiss, seed = 1234, m = 3, chi="all", list(se = "standard"))

On the issue of bootstrapping and bootstrap confidence intervals with MI. We have not implemented the method recommended by Wu and Jia (2013), but I'll put it on the TODO list for runMI.

Alex

messages.subject: Re: Moderated mediation and latent variables
parts:
Thanks for catching my mistaken assumption, Alex.

Helene -- In the meantime, I believe Wu & Jia found that the MI-bootstrap results are similar to FIML-and-bootstrap.  So you could just use FIML and specify bootstrap SEs.  If you are concerned about important excluded variables from your imputation model, you can include them using the saturated-correlates approach.  The semTools function auxiliary() helps automate this process, and its help page includes a reference to the paper that describes it.

Terry
